hypotheses.title: Stage 5 and CFG passes create a fresh semtypes.Context per function body and per lambda, discarding subtype memo caches
hypotheses.issue: semtypes.Context holds the subtype/emptiness memo tables (_listMemo, _mappingMemo, _functionMemo, comparable/filler memos, interner) whose keys are global interned BDD keys, so results are valid for the whole type environment. ResolvePrivateNodes spawns one unbounded goroutine per function declaration and resolveFunctionBody creates semtypes.ContextFrom(p.typeEnv()) for each; resolveLambdaFunctionExpr / resolveInferredLambdaFunctionExpr create yet another fresh context per lambda (same goroutine as the enclosing body), and resolveMatchStatement / matchClausePatternType create one per match. The CFG pass (cfg.Build spawns a goroutine per function/method/lambda; analyzeFunctionBody calls ContextFrom per body) does the same. Consequently identical checks (R1 <: R2, R1 <: json, <: map<anydata>, function(int) returns int <: expected) are recomputed from scratch in every function: IsSubtype->IsEmpty->bddEvery/bddDiff is ~13-15% of CPU, and ContextFrom alone allocated ~256 MB (1.27M objects) on corpus/bench/10-bench/expressions-v.bal (49% from CFG analyzeFunctionBody, 35% resolveFunctionBody, 15% lambdas). Unbounded goroutine-per-function spawning also adds runtime.copystack cost. Other per-body ContextFrom sites with the same pattern: semantics/internal/cfg/cfg_analyzer.go, uninitialized_var_analyzer.go, desugar/desugar.go:212, desugar/expression.go, desugar/query_expression.go (not touched by the prototype). A Context is not goroutine-safe, so reuse must be per worker.

reproducer.command: python3 gen.py 10000 fns10k.bal && go build -o bal ./cli/cmd && GOMAXPROCS=1 /usr/bin/time -v ./bal run --stats-oneline fns10k.bal ; ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> fns10k.bal

hypotheses.fix_approach: Replace the goroutine-per-function spawning in ResolvePrivateNodes and cfg.Build with a bounded worker pool (min(GOMAXPROCS, jobs) workers draining a pre-filled channel); each worker creates one semtypes.Context and passes it to every function body it processes (resolveFunctionBody / analyzeFunctionBody now take tyCtx as a parameter). Lambdas and match-statement helpers reuse the enclosing resolver's t.typeContext() instead of ContextFrom. Pitfalls: a Context must never be shared across goroutines (make test-race clean); field initializers are resolved serially before the pool starts so they can use the package resolver's context. Further headroom: the remaining per-body ContextFrom sites in cfg_analyzer.go, uninitialized_var_analyzer.go and desugar were not changed. Wall-time gains at default parallelism are partially masked by GC/noise; measure stage times with GOMAXPROCS=1 for stable numbers. A first benchmark run was flagged unreliable (time CV 5.3%); the re-run on an idle machine was a clear improvement.

notes: Exploration also ruled out: monomorphization cache keying (gain lands in BIR gen, out of scope), an IsSubtype result cache keyed on SemTypeInterner (Intern does linear scans -> quadratic), and SymbolSpace/CompilerEnvironment RLock traffic (~1% CPU).
